projectDesc.p: Encoded for the Experiencing War web site for the Veterans History Project.

samplingDecl.p: The recording of the interview with Curtis Gadd:: was digitized.

editorialDecl.p: This transcription was encoded with minimal changes to the original text in an effort to preserve original content and idiosyncrasies of the person interviewed. Period language and terminology are also retained. Encoding is literal with regard to the transcriptionist's capitalization, punctuation, and spelling. Spelling errors are indicated with [sic]; however, recurring errors in spelling within a single document have been marked the first time and not subsequently.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Where were you living in 1941?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: How old were you then, in '41?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So when did you go in the service, before Pearl Harbor?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: What do you remember of that date, December 7, '41?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So you heard it from someone; you didn't actually hear it on the radio?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: What was your reaction when you heard that?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: You didn't get caught up and want to run out and sign up the next day?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So you were drafted probably what, '42?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: What made you decide to do that, to sign up?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: All right. What can you tell me, any memorable incidents during your training there at Fort Benning?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Did you personally get the stuff pounded out of you?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Do you remember your first jump during training?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Mm-hmm.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So then your training was done and you were ready to head overseas after that?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: All in one tent?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Like what?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: During your training, what was it like to be thrown into a situation with guys from all over the country, when you probably hadn't seen much of that before?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Are those guys you went through the service with?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: In the 17th?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So when did you go overseas?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Yeah. Explain that.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: All right.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So tell me about the job of a pathfinder.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: I don't know if I saw that episode, but I know what you're talking about, yeah.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Great.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Right.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Would you go it alone as a pathfinder or a small group of guys?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Would go in -- how far before the main landing?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Did the Germans have a way of scoping in where that radar was set up that you set up on the ground?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: You must have been in England for several months before you went to the continent?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: What was life like in England there when you were there before you went to the continent?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So when did you first go to the continent from there? Was it sometime after D-Day? Obviously after D-Day, but...

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Mm-hmm.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So you were in England for approximately a year and a half?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: I'm talking about when did you go into action in France, Germany, whatever?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Yeah, I thought you mentioned that.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Did you drop into that battle?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Trucked in, landed in Le Harve or something or somewhere in France or Belgium?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Mm-hmm.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Sometime around October, November, something?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: But you had to ask.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So did you get along with the French people then?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: I know who you're talking about, but I can't remember his name either.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So were the maquis fighting the Germans though?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: But not for the allies?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Was it Patan?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Right. So you got along with them?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: For the most part, with the French.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Am I guessing correctly, if I'm guessing?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: That's what I'm guessing. They didn't have the will to really fight.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Do you remember your first day in combat?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Was that during the Bulge?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So were you in Belgium then at that time or still in France?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: I'm sure you do.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So what other memories do you have of the Bulge?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Not with it that long.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: What was your rank?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So how did that happen? How did you keep going up and down?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Started the day as a buck sergeant and went down to a buck private?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: How did you regain the right then?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Because they knew you were a good soldier probably. So for the most part did you get along with the officers?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Let me take a guess BOQ, battalion officers quarters?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Bachelor officer quarters.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Of course, when we were in Camp Forrest, Tennessee or someplace, we all had -- I had my wife down there. I was one of the few married. I was an old man, I was 22 years old and married. Don't forget, the average age of paratroopers was only 18 1/2. It wasn't even 19, because so many lied about their age to get in. We had them in there at 15 years old. And then we'd find them and mom would come and get him or something like -- but there was a lot that went to combat that was under 18, an awful lot of them. And you consider a guy today -- well, look at the maturity of kids today, the maturity in those days and how rapidly you matured. A company commander, he's got -- well, an airborne is 176 men. He's 22 years old. We have a battalion commander, who's a lieutenant colonel, and he's got almost 600 or 700. Their destiny is under him. Now, that's maturity, and you matured in a hurry.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: How many combat jumps did you make?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Just the one into Germany?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Before we get to that, is there anything else that you remember at the Bulge that you wanted included?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Well, I have talked to one other local veteran in the 17th, though, a guy that lives east of town here, east of Cleveland.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: A guy named Robert Cable.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Bob Cable, as in cable.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: C-a-b-l-e.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: He was 17th Airborne. He was a glider trooper. He went in on gliders.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Bob Cable.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: I don't think we talked about that, so I don't know if he does or not. He lives in Middlefield.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So you mentioned you were married. Do you remember getting letters from home?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Whatever your rank was that week?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So was it almost to the point of gouging the service men?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Nobody was watching over that?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So this was near Fort Benning?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Fort Bragg in North Carolina?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So did you get many packages and things when you were overseas from your wife?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Were you able to write back much to her?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: After the Bulge, you were in France until March?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Into Germany?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: I can fill that in from a history book.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So tell me about that. You were a pathfinder on that mission?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Okay. How did it actually happen?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So what else can you tell me about that campaign when you jumped into Germany?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: And for the most part you did not encounter a lot of German resistance when you went in?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: What was the civilian population like in Germany when you went in there?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: They weren't afraid of the Americans or the allies?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Because that's what they said would happen.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Sure.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Did you lose any buddies?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Did you lose any buddies?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So what was the rest of the campaign in Germany like then after that?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: The rest of the campaign in Germany up to VE Day, was it relatively quiet?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Where were you on VE Day?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: I'm not sure if I do know.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Mm-hmm.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So was there a bunch of celebration on VE Day for you?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Wow.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So how much longer were you in Germany then after VE Day?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Was there any possibility you were going to be sent to the Pacific Campaign?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So did you actually hear of the news of the dropping of the bombs before that?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: What was it like on the boat at that moment, pretty wild celebration?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So what was your reunion with your wife like?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Mm-hmm.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Well, when you got back.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: I guess I'm missing something. What's the Wasserman and Kahn test results?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: So you proved that you were clean?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Were those the names of the doctors who developed the tests? How did they get their names?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Are they named for the doctors who developed the test, Wasserman and Kahn?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: I never heard that before. I've heard of the tests. I've never heard of the name.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Wasserman and Kahn. Did you -- go ahead.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Did you have something -- go ahead.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: When you think about that experience overseas, does any particularly vivid memory come to mind?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: What was going through your mind? Were you thinking that, "I've got to get out of here"?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: But it must have been a reaction; it must have been frostbite, right?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Well, very good. You think that covers it?

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Right. Sure.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: Wow.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: You do your job.

sp.speaker: Thomas Swope
sp.p: What can you tell me about when you went in and did that recording?
